scope: JoyAI 27.5-second flower-arranging robot-layer temporal stabilization and persistent-grasp restoration
summary: The multi-anchor consensus plus recursive appearance-state challenger is accepted for the frozen camera-frame visual contract: source-motion-aligned robot-layer jitter mean falls 8.216%, late hand-edge failures fall from 22/180 to 0/180, late projected contact is 11/11, and persistent visual grasp plus erasure rejection are 147/147. Overall status remains PARTIAL because the evidence is one 2-D scene without metric depth, force closure, or real execution.
evidence: The final 1280x720 MP4 decodes 660/660 frames at 24 FPS for 27.5 seconds and has SHA-256 a63237403e2b010444ad885277dd5b06f75370f9c4dcbde418732b641b3099a8.
The frozen long-video audit reuses the v5 incumbent limits verbatim and passes every image-space gate plus color, topology, contact-removal, and structure-ghost attacks.

At or after 20 seconds, projected contact recall is 11/11 and hand-edge lower-gate violations are 0/180; the source-observed hold interval passes 147/147 persistent visual-grasp frames and 147/147 erasure attacks.

Across 161 declared risk transitions, layer-warp MAE mean improves from 7.075632 to 6.494297, p95 from 20.724682 to 19.161703, and maximum from 29.420279 to 26.685484; transitions above 20 decrease from 10 to 7.
Consensus, recursive state update, and bounded hand-detail projection take 268.145181, 108.835392, and 62.385857 seconds respectively; each stage preserves its declared non-editable locks exactly.
lessons: Long-video flicker is better modeled as a persistent appearance-state estimation error than as independent bad frames.
Anchor consensus removes donor disagreement while a causal recursive update suppresses residual temporal innovation without changing flower, background, contact, or endpoint locks.
Hand-detail recovery must be a bounded current-frame projection followed by a complete encoded adversarial audit; pre-encode success alone is insufficient.
limitations: The 8.216% jitter reduction is measured only on 161 transitions in three risk windows of one scene.
Projected overlap and occlusion bridging do not establish 3-D hand-stem depth, contact force, or force closure.
The generated robot is a visual replacement, not evidence of real robot execution.
next_actions: Replicate the frozen risk-window audit on independent flower-arranging scenes before treating the appearance-state method as a general learned capability.
Keep physical promotion separate until calibrated depth, telemetry, or force evidence is acquired.
